Anya: bringing up tangram11b (int4) Canary on dedicated pool, getting OOMs for somewhat small payloads :grimacing:
Carl: details? batch size / max_new_tokens / prompt length? :eyes:
Anya: batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=6000, avg prompt ~1.2k tokens. OOM stack points to KV allocation.
Marisol: tangram has big KV per layer, int4 doesn't reduce KV size. We saw frag with jemalloc earlier.
Zhou: try lowering max_new_tokens default to 1024 for the canary and enable kv_trim on expired contexts.
Anya: ok will try - changing runtime config now and requeueing canary.
deploy-bot: Canary tangram11b-int4 deployed to pool-gamma at 2065432135.
Anya: still seeing mem spikes during bursts, despite max_new_tokens=1024. attaching small trace excerpt:
```
OOM at allocate(134217728) kv_cache.cpp:412
thread 0x7f12bd filled with 0x40 pointers
free_pages: 12MB contiguous not found
jemalloc: arena 3 fragmentation 28%
```
Carl: fragmentation is high. What's the LRU retention window? If warmup priming holds prefixes, you can get many small allocations over time.
Marisol: Config we used earlier that helped for other 11b: 
```
model:
  max_new_tokens: 1024
  kv_trim: true
  kv_trim_window: 30s
  continuous_batching: true
  batch_prealloc: 64MB
```
Zhou: Also try enabling `prefer_large_pages: true` for the canary nodes (reduces internal fragmentation).
Anya: applied kv_trim + prefer_large_pages, restarted canary 2065432160.
Anya: initial improvement, mem spike amplitude down ~40% but still occasional OOM at tail latencies.
Carl: check sequence lengths distribution: if a few requests hit 6k while most are small, batching can cause the allocator to reserve based on max in batch. Consider adaptive windowing: group by length or use dynamic_max_new_tokens per-request.
Marisol: canary telemetry shows those OOMs align with rare long user prompts from internal tests. Suggest a fallback: if required max_new_tokens > 2048, route to larger-pool or degrade to int8 variant.
Zhou: add routing rule: route requests with requested_new_tokens>2048 -> tag:large-window; policy: low-priority or int8-fallback.
Anya: created PR for routing rule and adjusted default max_new_tokens to 1500 in model profile. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/tangram11b-canary/234
deploy-bot: PR merged and rollout started at 2065432200.
Carl: follow-up: run jemalloc stats dump periodically to detect growing fragmentation and trigger compaction (or restart). We automated that for other 11b — saved a patch restart per week.
Marisol: file an eval to compare quant-int4 vs int8 quality at 1500 tokens and cost delta. Want to know if fallback hurts latency/quality.
Anya: logging follow-up notes in the ticket. Action items: 1) keep kv_trim on, 2) enable prefer_large_pages, 3) routing rule for >2048, 4) schedule weekly jemalloc compaction check. I'll own the rollout monitoring.
Zhou: thanks. If we still see OOMs after 24h, we can enable soft-kv-eviction to bound memory at cost of some extra compute.
Anya: noted. will report back tomorrow with 24h stats. :thumbsup:
